## Appearance

Thirza possesses a tall, slender frame with sharp angles, a lean figure, and a pale face with lined cheeks. Her hands are rough and calloused from labor. Her dark hair, which gradually silvered over time, has turned snow-white and is bound tightly in a firm bun at the back. Though once at risk of total blindness, her failing eyesight eventually stabilized; while her eyes will fail no further, they are unlikely to improve significantly from their current state.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Surprised P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015), [v2 VIII Thirza Adopts Twins P3](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0003), [v2 XII A Jonah Day P39](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0039), [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P4](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0004), [v2 XV The Beginning of Vacation P43](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0043), +4 more_

## Personality

Characterized by a composed, practical, and rational demeanor, this individual maintains a rigid and unyielding sense of morality. She displays a stern, strict, and fault-finding nature, frequently attaching moral lessons to her speech while strictly disapproving of eating quickly with large bites. Despite her restrained and pessimistic disposition, she possesses a subtle sense of humor and has grown softer, mellow, and kinder over time. Driven by an uncompromising commitment to her duty, she holds a deep affection for [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md), despite feeling anxious over the girl's spontaneous nature and having difficulty expressing her own emotions verbally. Additionally, she loathes cats, lacks a refined appreciation of beauty, and steadfastly refuses on principle to express opinions about ministers. Her known talents include making famous homemade currant wine, preparing yellow plum preserves, and crafting circular braided rugs.

## History

Thirza Abernethy lived at [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) for sixty years after reaching adulthood, having spent her childhood being called a homely child by her aunt and wallpapering a spare room with the help of [Obed Abernethy](../character/obed-abernethy.md). When [Obed](../character/obed-abernethy.md) brought home a young orphan girl named [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) instead of a boy, Thirza initially insisted on sending her back, though she soon sympathized with the girl's past and agreed to keep her. Despite her strict guidance and skepticism toward Nell's imaginative antics, Thirza gradually grew deeply fond of her. Over the years, Thirza mistakenly accused [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) of stealing her mother's inherited amethyst brooch before finding it caught in her own shawl, supported Nell's education after Obed's death, and agreed to take in two orphaned twins, [Robin](../character/robin-farrow.md) and [Lucy](../character/lucy.md) Farrow. Facing severe vision loss, Thirza invited Mrs. Agatha Sowerby to live at [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) so [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) could attend college. Years later, after seeing [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) marry [Hugh Carrow](../character/hugh-carrow.md), Thirza traveled to [Seven Gulls Harbor](../codex/places.md#seven-gulls-harbor) to assist during Nell's pregnancy and provided comfort when Nell's firstborn infant died.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Surprised P31](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0031), [v1 CHAPTER III. ## Quotes

> "At minimum, provide me with someone native born. A risk will exist, regardless of whom we obtain. Nevertheless, my mind will be more at ease and my night’s sleep will be sounder if we obtain a born Canadian."
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Agatha Sowerby Is Surprised P23](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0023)

> "No. A boy is what we need to assist Obed on the farm. To us, a girl would be useless. Remove your hat. On the hall table, I’ll place it along with your bag."
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised P30](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0030)

> "Now, strip off your clothes as fast as possible and get into bed. In a little while, I’ll return to fetch the candle. Leaving you to extinguish it on your own is too risky. It’s probable you’d burn down the house."
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised P44](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0044)

> "Obed Abernethy, my belief is that you have been enchanted by that child! It is as clear as day to me that your desire is to retain her."
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER III. Thirza Abernethy Is Surprised P61](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0061)

> "Obed Abernethy, my surprise at you is great. Though aware of Nell’s terrible conduct, you still defend her! Next, I expect you will claim that no punishment whatsoever should be given to her!"
>
> — Thirza Abernethy — [v1 CHAPTER X. Nell’s Apology P2](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0002)

## Relationships

### [Agatha Sowerby](../character/agatha-sowerby.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/agatha-sowerby--thirza-abernethy.md)

[Agatha Sowerby](../character/agatha-sowerby.md) is a longstanding neighbor and friend of Thirza Abernethy, frequently visiting [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) to exchange news and offer opinions. Though they travel into town together, their interactions often involve [Agatha](../character/agatha-sowerby.md) raising doubts about Thirza's household decisions or making blunt criticisms, such as mocking Nell's appearance. Nevertheless, Thirza works to maintain harmony between their households, accompanying [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) to deliver apologies when tensions flare.

### [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/nell-harcourt--thirza-abernethy.md)

Thirza serves as a strict yet loving guardian and maternal figure to [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) after initially attempting to return the orphan girl to [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia). Although Thirza enforces discipline, religious studies, and simple attire, she grows deeply fond of [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md), providing guidance, emotional support, and defense against outside criticism. Over time, their dynamic evolves into a warm, bond where they manage household affairs and handle family challenges as close companions.

### [Obed Abernethy](../character/obed-abernethy.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/obed-abernethy--thirza-abernethy.md)

[Obed Abernethy](../character/obed-abernethy.md) was Thirza's brother, with whom she lived at [Grey Shutters](../codex/places.md#grey-shutters) and co-parented [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) until his health began to fail. ### [Robin Farrow](../character/robin-farrow.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/robin-farrow--thirza-abernethy.md)

[Robin Farrow](../character/robin-farrow.md) is Thirza's third cousin once removed, whom she took in as a guardian alongside his twin sister. Thirza actively enforces discipline against his energetic mischief, dishonesty, and pranks, sending him to bed without dinner while attempting to teach him proper moral behavior.

_Sources: [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P32](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0032), [v2 VIII Thirza Adopts Twins P1](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0001), [v2 VIII Thirza Adopts Twins P30](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0030), +17 more_

### [Pembroke](../character/pembroke.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/pembroke--thirza-abernethy.md)

Mrs. [Pembroke](../character/pembroke.md) is an acquaintance of Thirza whose daughter Isolde is close friends with [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md). Their relationship experienced severe strain when [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) accidentally served Isolde elderberry wine, leading Mrs. [Pembroke](../character/pembroke.md) to rebuff Thirza's attempts to clear up the misunderstanding until the matter was eventually forgiven.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P0](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0000), [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P14](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0014), [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), +14 more_
